desc: Verify the two-pointer greedy on random small arrays by brute force to ensure correctness.
Precompute next[i] = smallest j > i with A[j] >= 2*A[i] (or N+1) using O(N) two-pointer from the right.
Implement a per-query O(R-L) simulation: compute M = max{i ≤ R | next[i] ≤ R} via binary search on next (non-decreasing), set T = min(R, M), then run two-pointer to count matches.
Design and implement a segment tree where each node stores state f(x) = (matches, new_bottom_pointer) for a given incoming bottom pointer x, and merge two child states to answer queries in O(log N).
Optimize the query processing to O(log N) using the segment tree, handling the dependence on R via the next[] array and the non-decreasing property.
Test the optimized solution on the provided samples and random cases against the brute-force baseline.
